structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single reviewable CANDIDATE architecture/design document for the Pre-Python gate at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/scheduling-and-recovery.md, limited to scheduling, concurrency, cancellation, retry, recovery, ownership, and ambiguous-worker semantics, using cited existing authority/evidence without implementing or approving Python architecture.
structuredContent.summary: The packet has clear scope, authority, exclusions, acceptance criteria, and verification expectations. It authorizes documentation-only work, identifies source baselines and binding architecture constraints, and explicitly treats unresolved material Founder decisions as content to record rather than blockers to drafting unless they prevent a candidate from being written. The work is cohesive and independently reviewable as one design artifact.
implementation_unknowns: Locate and accurately map the cited Node dispatcher, worktree-manager, lifecycle tests, B-DISP rows D17/D18/D31, and other named baselines into source/invariant mappings without treating them as broader authority than stated.
Determine from the cited material which scheduling/recovery semantics are established evidence, which are candidate extrapolations, and which must be labeled as unresolved Founder decisions.
Draft successful and failing examples that are faithful to the bounded authority and do not imply implementation readiness or API stability.
Ensure documentation checker/path coverage expectations are satisfied for the new artifact and any local packet/readiness evidence allowed by the task.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable through review of the produced markdown artifact and any allowed local packet/readiness evidence: it must cover global/profile/repository admission bounds, reserve-before-await ownership, dependency handling, cancellation ordering, finite retry/backoff/jitter, crash recovery, ambiguous-worker handling, preservation of evidence, and prohibition on cleaning live/unowned resources. A single independent content review can meaningfully judge whether the document traces claims to the supplied authority, labels candidate semantics and unresolved Founder decisions, stays within documentation-only scope, and avoids implicit adoption of neighboring documents or implementation behavior.
material_risks: The author may accidentally convert candidate design language into adopted architecture or implementation authority, contrary to the packet’s limits.
The document could overgeneralize from Node bootstrap behavior and historical evidence into Python capability claims or stable API semantics.
Cross-document dependencies may tempt implicit adoption of neighboring candidate contracts instead of explicitly recording unresolved choices.
Scheduling/recovery semantics touch operational state, authority, and resource preservation; vague wording could create later ambiguity around live or ambiguous resources.
Founder-review-required decisions must be identified precisely rather than silently decided for convenience.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the bounded candidate design document and allowed local readiness/packet evidence, using the cited sources as traceable inputs and clearly marking candidate semantics, limitations, examples, and unresolved Founder decisions.
structuredContent.rationale: READY is the controlling disposition because the task defines a coherent documentation-only outcome, supplies governing architecture authority and baselines, excludes implementation and operational side effects, and gives observable acceptance criteria. Remaining uncertainty is ordinary engineering/documentation research about mapping cited evidence and wording candidate contracts, not unresolved owner intent. The work does not need semantic splitting because scheduling, cancellation, retry, recovery, and ownership form one coupled concurrency/recovery policy whose review verdict can be applied to a single artifact; failures are expected to be localized to that document.
